prompt: Order: ba / ka / na  (→ 'are you ... yet?')
explanation: Enclitic order: monosyllabic pronoun (ka) → na/pa → ba.

prompt: Order: kumain / ba / na / kayo  (→ 'Have you all eaten yet?')
explanation: na before ba; the two-syllable pronoun kayo goes after all monosyllabic particles.

prompt: Order: umalis / siya / na / daw  (→ 'They say he already left.')
explanation: na → daw (monosyllabic particles) → siya (two-syllable pronoun) last.

prompt: Order: gusto / lang / ko  (→ 'I just want (it).')
explanation: Monosyllabic pronoun ko comes right after the predicate, before lang (two syllables).

prompt: Order: bakit / tinanong / mo / pa / ba  (→ 'Why did you even still ask?')
explanation: Enclitics attach to the first word (bakit): mo → pa → ba, then the verb.

prompt: Order: hindi / ako / pa / nakakain  (→ 'I haven't eaten yet.')
explanation: After hindi: pa (na/pa slot) before the two-syllable pronoun ako, then the verb.

prompt: Order: pupunta / din / ako  (→ 'I'm going too.')
explanation: Monosyllabic particle din before two-syllable pronoun ako. rin after vowels is the textbook form; din is common in speech.

prompt: Order: kain / na / tayo  (→ 'Let's eat now.')
explanation: na comes before the two-syllable pronoun tayo. Root 'kain' alone works as an invitation.

prompt: Order: nandito / na / ba / siya  (→ 'Is he here already?')
explanation: na → ba → siya: monosyllabic particles first, two-syllable pronoun last.

prompt: Order: ikaw / pala / 'yan  (→ 'Oh, it's you!')
explanation: pala (surprise/realization) follows the first word. 'yan = iyan (that).

prompt: Order: ayaw / ko / nga  (→ 'I said I don't want to.')
en: I said I don't want to.
explanation: ko (monosyllabic pronoun) first, then nga (two-syllable particle: insistence).

prompt: Order: ano / ba / 'yan  (→ 'What is that?!')
explanation: ba sits right after the question word; here it adds exasperation, not a yes/no question.

prompt: Order: nasaan / na / ba / siya  (→ 'Where is he now?')
explanation: Question word first, then na → ba → siya.

prompt: Order: kumain / ka / na / ba  (→ 'Have you eaten yet?')
explanation: Full order: ka → na → ba. Compare 'Kumain na ba kayo?' where two-syllable kayo goes last.

prompt: Order: sinabi / ko / na / sa'yo  (→ 'I already told you.')
explanation: ko → na; the non-enclitic phrase sa'yo (sa iyo) comes after all enclitics.

prompt: Order: hindi / mo / ba / alam  (→ 'Don't you know?')
explanation: Enclitics attach to hindi: mo → ba, then the predicate alam.

prompt: Order: late / na / naman / ako  (→ 'I'm late again.')
explanation: na → naman (two-syllable particle) → ako (two-syllable pronoun). 'na naman' = again, as usual.

prompt: Order: wala / kasi / ako / pera  (→ 'Because I have no money.')
explanation: Two-syllable particle kasi before two-syllable pronoun ako; ako takes -ng before pera.

prompt: Order: sige / na / nga  (→ 'Oh fine, go ahead.')
explanation: na (monosyllabic) → nga (two syllables). 'Sige na nga' = giving in reluctantly.

prompt: Order: tapos / ka / na / ba  (→ 'Are you done yet?')
explanation: ka → na → ba after the predicate tapos.

prompt: Order: uuwi / daw / siya / na / bukas  (→ 'He's going home tomorrow, they say.')
explanation: na → daw → siya; the adverb bukas is not an enclitic, so it comes last.

prompt: Order: ako / na / lang  (→ 'I'll just do it.')
explanation: Ako is the fronted predicate here; enclitics na → lang follow it.

prompt: Choose ang / ng / sa: Natutulog ___ bata.
explanation: ang marks the focus (topic) of the sentence: the thing the sentence is about.

prompt: Choose ang / ng / sa: Kumain ako ___ mangga.
explanation: With an actor-focus verb (kumain) the object is non-focus and takes ng.

prompt: Choose ang / ng / sa: Pupunta ako ___ mall.
explanation: sa marks location, direction, time and recipients.

prompt: Choose ang / ng / sa: Kinain ko ___ mangga.
explanation: Object-focus verb (kinain): the object is the focus → ang; the actor is in ng-form (ko).

prompt: Choose si / ni / kay: Dumating na ___ Marco.
explanation: si = ang for personal names. Plural: sina Marco at Ana.

prompt: Choose si / ni / kay: Ito ang kotse ___ Marco.
explanation: ni = ng for names: possessor or non-focus actor (Binili ni Marco).

prompt: Choose si / ni / kay: Ibinigay ko ___ Ana ang susi.
explanation: kay = sa for names: recipient or location ('kay Ana' = at Ana's place).

prompt: Make plural: Nakita ko ang bata.  (→ 'I saw the children.')
explanation: mga goes right after the marker: ang mga / ng mga / sa mga. The noun itself never changes.

prompt: Choose ng mga / sa mga: Nagbigay siya ng pagkain ___ bata.
explanation: Recipient = sa; plural adds mga after it: sa mga bata.

prompt: Choose ng mga / sa mga: Bumili ako ___ regalo para sa kanila.
explanation: Non-focus object = ng; plural adds mga: ng mga regalo.

prompt: Choose nasa / sa: ___ mall ako ngayon.
explanation: nasa = 'is at/in'; it is the predicate, no verb needed. Plain sa follows a verb: Pupunta ako sa mall.

prompt: Choose nasa / sa: Pupunta ako ___ Makati bukas.
explanation: After a motion verb use sa. nasa only when the location itself is the predicate: Nasa Makati ako.

prompt: Choose nasa / sa: ___ bag ko ang wallet ko.
explanation: Location predicate: Nasa bag ko ang wallet ko = my wallet is in my bag.

prompt: Rewrite with ay-inversion: Mabait ang titser.
explanation: ay puts the topic first; formal/written. Spoken Manila Tagalog is predicate-first: Mabait ang titser.

prompt: Fill: ___ pera ako.  (I have money.)
explanation: may + bare noun directly, no ng: May pera ako. Meron/mayroon instead takes a linker: Meron akong pera.

prompt: Rewrite with meron: May pera ako.
explanation: meron/mayroon stands alone, so the pronoun moves next to it and takes -ng. 'Meron' is the spoken form.

prompt: Fill: ___ akong pera.  (I have no money.)
explanation: wala = none/not have; the pronoun gets the -ng linker: Wala akong pera.

prompt: Choose ng / nang: Kumain siya ___ mabilis.
explanation: nang links a verb to how it's done (adverb of manner) and means 'when'. ng marks nouns: kumain ng kanin.

prompt: Choose ng / nang: Bumili ako ___ kape.
explanation: ng before a noun (object or possessor). nang only for manner, 'when', and na+ng contractions.

prompt: Choose ng / nang: Wala ___ tao sa opisina.  (No one is at the office anymore.)
explanation: nang here is 'na' (already) + linker -ng: wala na + ng tao → wala nang tao. Not the noun marker ng.

prompt: Choose ng / nang: Umalis siya ___ dumating ako.
explanation: nang = 'when' joining two clauses in the past. Spoken Manila often says 'noong dumating ako' too.

prompt: Choose ang / ng: Gusto ko ___ kape.  (I want some coffee.)
explanation: ng = coffee in general / some coffee; ang = that specific coffee (Gusto ko ang kape na 'to). ng is the default.

prompt: Convert: ako (ang-form) → ng-form
explanation: Sets: ako / ko / akin. The ng-form marks possessor or non-focus actor: bahay ko, ginawa ko.

prompt: Convert: ikaw / ka → ng-form
explanation: Sets: ikaw(ka) / mo / iyo. Bahay mo = your house; ginawa mo = you did it.

prompt: Convert: siya → ng-form
explanation: Sets: siya / niya / kanya. Spoken and texted as nya.

prompt: Convert: kami → sa-form
explanation: Sets: kami / namin / amin. 'Sa amin' = to us / at our place.

prompt: Convert: sila → ng-form
explanation: Sets: sila / nila / kanila. Bahay nila = their house.

prompt: Convert: tayo → sa-form
explanation: Sets: tayo / natin / atin. 'Sa atin' = to us (including you); 'atin 'to' = this is ours.

prompt: Convert: kayo → ng-form
explanation: ninyo is the full form; spoken Manila says niyo / nyo. Also the polite singular 'you'.

prompt: Say 'I love you' using the one word that replaces ko + ikaw
explanation: kita = ko + ka/ikaw (I → you). Never 'mahal ko ikaw'. Also: Tatawagan kita = I'll call you.

prompt: Fill: Tatawagan ___ bukas.  (I'll call you tomorrow.)
explanation: Whenever the actor is 'I' (ko) and the focus is 'you' (ka), they fuse into kita.

prompt: Choose kami / tayo: Kain ___!  (Let's eat — including the listener)
explanation: tayo = we including you; kami = we but not you.

prompt: Choose kami / tayo: Aalis na ___, bye!  (We're leaving — not you)
explanation: kami excludes the listener: we're leaving, you stay. tayo would mean 'let's leave'.

prompt: Choose niya / nila: Binili ___ ang bahay.  (They bought the house.)
explanation: niya = he/she, nila = they. Object-focus verb binili → actor takes ng-form.

prompt: Rewrite with aking: ang bahay ko
explanation: Two possessives: noun + ko/mo/niya (everyday) or aking/iyong/kanyang + noun (formal, emphatic). Default: bahay ko.

prompt: Choose ikaw / ka: ___ ba si Lloyd?  (Are you Lloyd?)
explanation: ikaw starts a sentence or stands alone as predicate; ka is the enclitic form after the predicate: Lloyd ka ba?

prompt: Choose ikaw / ka: Saan ___ pupunta?
explanation: After a predicate or question word, use enclitic ka, never ikaw.

prompt: Fill: Para ___ ito.  (This is for you.)
explanation: sa-form pronouns after para/sa: para sa'yo, para sa akin, para sa kanya. sa'yo = sa iyo.

prompt: Fill: ___ ba 'to?  (Is this yours?)
explanation: Possession as predicate uses sa-forms: Sa'yo ba 'to? Akin 'to. Kanya 'yun.

prompt: Translate (everyday form): his phone
explanation: Everyday possessive: noun + niya. 'Kanyang phone' is formal. Texted: phone nya.

prompt: Join with the linker: maganda + babae
explanation: After a vowel, add -ng to the first word: maganda → magandang.

prompt: Join with the linker: masarap + pagkain
explanation: After a consonant other than n, use a separate 'na'.

prompt: Join with the linker: bago + kotse
explanation: Vowel ending → -ng. Works with any modifier + noun pair.

prompt: Join with the linker: mabait + tao
explanation: Consonant ending (t) → separate na.

prompt: Join (noun first): bata + mabait
explanation: Order can flip; the linker always goes on the first word: mabait na bata = batang mabait.

prompt: Join: gusto ko + kumain
explanation: The linker also joins pseudo-verbs to verbs; it lands on the pronoun: gusto kong, ayaw niyang, pwede bang.

prompt: Join: kailangan ko + umuwi
explanation: kailangan + ko + -ng + infinitive. Same with dapat: Dapat kang matulog.

prompt: Join: iyon + bata  (→ 'that child' / spoken 'yung')
explanation: After n, the n becomes ng: iyon → iyong. Spoken Manila: 'yung bata. Same with iyan → iyang ('yang bata).

prompt: Join: wala + ako + pera
explanation: The linker attaches to the word right before the noun. Enclitic ako slips in: Wala akong pera, not 'Walang ako pera'.

prompt: Join: dalawa + anak
explanation: Numbers take the linker like adjectives: isang, dalawang, tatlong, apat na, limang.

prompt: Join: pwede ba + sumama ako
explanation: Enclitics ba and ako go after pwede; ako takes -ng before the verb.

prompt: Form the adjective from the root ganda (beauty)
explanation: ma- + root = adjective: ganda→maganda, sarap→masarap, bait→mabait, init→mainit.

prompt: Compare: 'Makati is more expensive than Pasig.'
tl: Mas mahal ang Makati kaysa sa Pasig.
en: Makati is more expensive than Pasig.
explanation: mas + adjective ... kaysa sa + noun. Spoken: 'Mas mahal sa Makati kaysa sa Pasig' (it's pricier in Makati).
accept_tl: Mas mahal ang Makati kaysa Pasig.
Mas mahal sa Makati kaysa sa Pasig.

prompt: Superlative: 'the most delicious'
explanation: pinaka- + full adjective (keep ma-): pinakamasarap, pinakamaganda, pinakamahal.

prompt: Intensify with napaka-: maganda → 'very beautiful'
explanation: napaka- + ROOT (drop ma-): napakaganda, napakasarap, napakainit.

prompt: Intensify with sobrang: mahal → 'super expensive'
explanation: sobrang + adjective is the everyday spoken intensifier: sobrang init, sobrang traffic, sobrang sarap.

prompt: Exclaim 'How beautiful!' using ang + root
explanation: Ang + root = exclamation: Ang ganda! Ang sarap! Ang mahal! Add ng/ni for the thing: Ang ganda ng view.

prompt: Pluralize the adjective: maganda (several beautiful girls)
explanation: Plural ma- adjectives double the first syllable of the root: magaganda, masasarap, mababait. Optional; mga alone is fine.

prompt: Translate: 'the beautiful girls'
explanation: Plural adjective + linker + noun. 'Ang mga magandang babae' is also fine; don't double up both unless emphatic.

prompt: Translate: 'a bit expensive'
explanation: medyo + adjective = somewhat/kind of. Medyo malayo, medyo late.

prompt: Translate: 'super delicious' (use napaka-)
explanation: napaka- takes the root sarap, not masarap. Spoken alternative: sobrang sarap.

prompt: Compare with a name: 'Marco is taller than Lloyd.'
tl: Mas matangkad si Marco kaysa kay Lloyd.
explanation: kaysa sa + common noun, kaysa kay + name (kaysa kina + several names). Spoken often drops to 'kaysa kay'.

prompt: Translate: 'It's more delicious here.'
explanation: mas works alone without kaysa when the comparison is understood from context.

prompt: Make it a yes/no question: Pupunta ka.
explanation: ba makes a yes/no question; it sits after the first enclitics (ka).

prompt: Choose hindi / wala / huwag / ayaw: ___ ako pupunta.  (I'm not going.)
explanation: hindi negates verbs, adjectives, identity. wala = none/not have. huwag = don't (command). ayaw = don't want.

prompt: Choose hindi / wala / huwag / ayaw: ___ akong pera.
explanation: Existence and possession are negated with wala, never hindi.

prompt: Choose hindi / wala / huwag / ayaw: ___ kang umalis.  (Don't leave.)
explanation: huwag + pronoun with -ng + infinitive: Huwag kang umalis. Spoken Manila: 'Wag kang umalis.

prompt: Choose hindi / wala / huwag / ayaw: ___ ko ng kape.  (I don't want coffee.)
explanation: ayaw + ko/mo/niya + ng noun, or -ng + verb: Ayaw kong kumain. Opposite: gusto.

prompt: Choose hindi / wala: ___ siya dito.  (He isn't here.)
explanation: Absence uses wala (Wala siya dito). 'Hindi siya dito' contrasts location: not here but somewhere else.

prompt: Add the tag 'right?': Mahal, ___?
explanation: 'di ba (hindi ba) = right? Goes at the end or the start: Di ba mahal 'yun?

prompt: Fix the word order: Pupunta ka saan?
explanation: Question words come first; the enclitic pronoun follows right after. 'Pupunta ka saan?' is only an echo question.

prompt: Ask 'What time?' (clock time)
explanation: kailan = when (day/date); anong oras = what time (clock). Anong oras ka uuwi?

prompt: Choose kailan / anong oras: ___ ang flight mo?  (which day)
explanation: kailan asks for a day or date; anong oras asks for a clock time.

prompt: Answer yes to: May pera ka ba?
explanation: may/meron questions are answered meron/wala, not oo/hindi. oo/hindi answer verb and adjective questions.

prompt: Answer no to: May pera ka ba?
explanation: wala answers may/meron questions in the negative. 'Wala, eh' softens it.

prompt: Answer no to: Pupunta ka ba?
explanation: hindi answers verb/adjective yes-no questions. Often with eh: Hindi, eh.

prompt: Answer yes to: Kumain ka na ba?
explanation: oo = yes; opo = polite yes (to elders/strangers). Natural answers repeat the verb with na: Kumain na.

prompt: Ask 'Who is that?' (a person)
explanation: sino = who (people), ano = what (things). Sino siya? Ano 'to?

prompt: Ask 'Where is the CR?'
explanation: nasaan = where is (location of something); saan = where + verb (Saan ka pupunta?). Manila speech also says 'Saan ang CR?'

prompt: Ask 'How much?' (price)
explanation: magkano = how much (price); ilan = how many. Magkano 'to? Ilan kayo?

prompt: Choose hindi / wala: ___ pa tapos.  (It's not done yet.)
explanation: hindi pa = not yet (verb/adjective). wala pa = none yet / not here yet: Wala pa siya.

prompt: Choose hindi / wala: ___ pa siya.  (He's not here yet.)
explanation: wala pa = hasn't arrived / none yet. Also 'Wala pa akong sahod' = I haven't been paid yet.

en: I'm just at the condo right now.
I bought a viand at the carinderia.

tl: Binili {{niya}} ang bagong phone sa Lazada.
en: He bought the new phone on Lazada.
I'm late again, the traffic is crazy.
Because I have no phone load.
I was late because of traffic on EDSA.
I'm going to the party too.
I have no money, lend me some first.

tl: Kumain siya {{nang}} mabilis kasi late na.
en: He ate quickly because it was late.
There's no one at the office anymore.
I went home when Mom called.

tl: Nakita ko ang {{mga}} bata sa park.
en: I saw the children at the park.
I'm not going to the meeting.
He's not here, he's in Cebu.
When are you coming back to the Philippines?
How much is a kilo of mangoes?
Who was that with you earlier?
The baby is still sleeping, don't be noisy.
We went to Tagaytay last weekend.

tl: Mas mahal ang Grab {{kaysa}} sa jeep.
en: Grab is more expensive than the jeep.

tl: Ito ang {{pinakamasarap}} na sisig sa Makati.
en: This is the best sisig in Makati.
The view from the rooftop is so beautiful!
The flowers in Baguio are beautiful.
